title: The Rookery
summary: The group reaches the Rookery, a crowded crossroads settlement where unusually distinct travelers and locals are everywhere. Eva initially reads the place as proof that the Cadre-like clustering is real.

panelPlan.text: The Rookery is dense, layered and human: boarding rooms, market tables, courtyards and family workshops around several dark fragments some travelers call Sunforge pieces.
Eva clocks Dylan Sheets, a masked herbal seller, an immaculate gambler and three other visually memorable people before they cross the first courtyard.
Marty Francis, the local host, greets Jessie by her vehicle and Brandon by the name Brandon gives him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: People who look like they walked out of six different stories.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: Good. Owe nobody money by sunset and we'll get along.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: I like whichever one of you is tired already.

title: Travelers See Types
summary: Marty dismantles Eva's first pattern by explaining who several 'Cadre' figures actually are: cousins, debtors, seasonal workers and people who have been returning to the Rookery for years.

panelPlan.text: Jessie claims Marty's title of 'the tired one' and tells Eva to stop counting. Eva immediately points out the silver mask as Marty walks her and Jessie through the market while doing real social work: settling a tab, checking on a sick vendor and carrying a parcel.
Each visually eccentric person Eva points out turns out to have a mundane reason for being there that locals have known for years.
Dylan Sheets appears at a workbench and laughs when Eva asks whether he came because of Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: Neral. Burned himself cooking mash twelve years ago. He's my cousin.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: Tova. Birds are hers. Debt is mine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You've been here five minutes and turned his cousin into a category.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I said nothing about a category.

title: The Man With Many Names
summary: Dylan has heard the story of 'the man with many names' through ordinary road gossip, but he knows Brandon's real name because Tomas at the Last Drop insisted on it.

panelPlan.text: Dylan and Brandon work side by side on a simple broken buckle or hand tool while Dylan remarks that the road categorizes people even more aggressively than Eva does. Keep the work tactile: leather, buckle, fingers and hand tools.
Dylan says the Brannock story has traveled farther than the group realized, accumulating Diaz and Merritt in some versions.
Eva brightens at the spread of names; Brandon points toward two travelers repeating the same rumor to different listeners.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dylan
dialogueInline.text: The road does worse. Says Brannock used to be a general.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: The road ought to pick one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: So the names are mixing together now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then the next town could call him anything and we won't know where it came from.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You keep saying 'our' like I signed up.

title: What Counts as a Sunforge
summary: Raina tries to classify the dark structures around the Rookery as multiple Sunforge fragments. Marty tells her locals do not consider them the same kind of thing and can trace different pieces to different histories.

panelPlan.text: Dylan's remark that Brandon at least sounds like himself gives Raina an opening to test something that is not about Brandon. She compares sketches of three black structures while Marty watches with increasing amusement.
Marty identifies one as an old roof support hauled in by his grandfather, one as a buried object no one has moved, and one as material salvaged from somewhere else entirely.
Eva realizes the traveler's single word may be flattening distinct local categories.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Then let's try something that isn't Brandon. Three Sunforge structures in one town.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: That one's the roof brace. That one's the old black thing. That one's the bench everybody hates.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Why does everybody hate the bench?

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: No. You're using one word for three things I have three stories about.

title: Why Everyone Came
summary: Several unusual travelers independently say they arrived because they heard 'something interesting' was happening in the Rookery. No one can identify a single source, but ordinary rumor is still sufficient to explain the convergence.

panelPlan.text: Eva asks Marty for the three local stories; Marty turns the method back on the travelers and asks where their own 'something interesting' story came from. At supper, answers overlap Answers overlap: a card game, a funeral, cheap rooms, a rumor about a buyer, somebody's cousin.
Raina tries to trace the phrase 'something interesting' backward and gets a loop of people citing each other.
Samuel recognizes the social shape immediately: expectation can aggregate without a mastermind.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: You want stories? Start with yours. Who told you something interesting was happening?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Bellweather heard about us after we left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: So nobody knows where it started.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Everybody knows who told them. That's different.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: You can try. You'll end up at somebody's cousin.

title: Constellations
summary: Marty warns Raina that travelers can turn unfamiliar people into a constellation because they do not know the histories between them. Raina accepts the criticism without abandoning the larger recurrence.

panelPlan.text: Brandon agrees to the investigation only after Marty promises it can wait until after supper. Later, on a rooftop or high gallery, Marty points down to people Eva had marked as separate oddities and narrates the mundane ties between them.
Raina closes one notebook but keeps another open, separating what is locally explained from what still lacks a source.
Brandon joins Eva and Jessie briefly, then leaves them talking after Eva asks whether weird places make weird people or merely reveal them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: All right. Start with Neral. You met a silver mask.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: I knew him when he had eyebrows.

dialogueInline.speaker: Marty Francis
dialogueInline.text: Didn't say it did. Stop charging me for the ones I can explain.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What if places like this just attract unusual people?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Maybe everybody looks strange when you don't know them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Brandon still looks unusual up close.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I liked this town better five minutes ago.
